tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after v2.3.1 went out to production (error rate 18%). v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, leaving regions on different versions for a short time. A retry finished the rollback. Current state: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and look into the orchestrator error during the rollback.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production (the broken one is v2.3.1). The first rollback attempt stopped with an orchestrator error after updating us-east, which left us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. I retried it, and all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0. The error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first request to open the incident timed out. I retried with the same idempotency key, which stops a retry from creating a second incident. The incident explains what went wrong, the rollback including the stalled first attempt, the current state, and two follow-ups: finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and looking into the orchestrator error.

v2.3.1's release candidate had also failed in staging, so it shouldn't be redeployed until the cause is found.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
The rollback stopped partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Running the same rollback again is safe, so I'll retry it once.
